name: Hippofolk
body:
Also known as floosberts, hippofolk are known as a highly regimented, effusive, sometimes petulant people who pride themselves in their skill at arms.

Physical

Hippofolk look like bipedal hippopotamuses. They are seven feet tall on average, with stout frames, but they are surprisingly light on their feet for their size.

Most hippofolk take a great deal of pride in their appearance, and are always dressed to impress. As their society is built around military traditions, a great number of them wear uniforms and insignia of some form or another at all times. Even civilian garb mimics military dress in its overall design, making it difficult for outsiders to know who is who—but a hippofolk can tell another hippofolk’s occupation and rank at a glance.

Social

Although the resemblance to hippos is uncanny, most hippofolk resent being compared to these lowly water-dwelling beasts. They insist that they are floosberts, not hippofolk, and will point that fact out to anyone who uses the wrong term—politely at first, and then with increasing aggression.

Floosbert society is extremely disciplined. It is organized around a tradition of hundreds of independent militias, each of which has its own military insignia, flags, customs, and traditions. In the distant past, these militias waged open warfare against each other—war that raged across the Multiverse. An armistice was eventually reached, and today floosberts will only fight each other if serving as mercenaries on opposite sides of a conflict—something they are all too happy to do, as they still jump at any chance to fight! Because of their wide-ranging war, hippofolk can be found throughout the Multiverse, although never in very large numbers. While each militia claims to be the only one that knows the location of the original floosbert homeworld, no one seems to actually have this knowledge. This has made the hippofolk a species of wandering mercenaries in search of the next battle. They gladly hire out their services to highest bidder if there is a promise of a good, honest fight. As professional soldiers, they do follow a code of conduct: they will not attack non-combatants or violate the terms of a treaty, and they will accept surrender if offered.

Alignment and Religion

Most hippofolk hew to a Lawful Neutral stance. They find comfort in conforming to their military rules and traditions, and enjoy the structure that this discipline brings to their lives.

Religion does not play a strong part in the lives of most hippofolk. Some will adopt a god of war, travel, or community to pray to in times of stress, but a hippofolk’s true faith is in their militia, and there is little room for dogma outside of that taught by their regiment.

Names

Hippofolk use only a single name, which they commonly decorate with many ranks and titles. They do not distinguish between male- and female-gendered names, and often choose what humans would consider surnames, titles, or object names. Some typical hippofolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d20):

Barnabus
Basil
Burton
Cecil
Cordell
Dean
Dericka
Ermintrude
Farley
Gemma
Giles
Keane
Morton
Parson
Renwick
Station
Tilda
Trista
Worsley
Yardley
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are powerful and perceptive, but your personality can rub people the wrong way. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Wis, –2 Cha [standard]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the hippofolk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aquan, Dwarven, Giant, Gnome, and Orc. (0)
Other Species Traits
Headfirst Charge If you charge and move at least 20 feet, you can make a head-butt attack at the end of the charge, dealing 2d4 bludgeoning damage + 1-1/2 times your Strength bonus. (2)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Military Training You gain a +1 species bonus on Profession (soldier) checks, and Profession (soldier) is always a class skill for you. (1)
Natural Armor You have thick skin that provides a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. (2)
Powerful Build Your physical stature allows you to function in many ways as if you were one size category larger. Whenever you are subject to a size modifier or special size modifier for a Combat Maneuver Bonus or Combat Maneuver Defense (such as during grapple checks, bull rush attempts, and trip attempts), you are treated as one size larger if doing so is advantageous to you. You are also considered to be one size larger when determining the damage of your unarmed strikes, and when determining whether a creature’s special attacks based on size (such as grab or swallow whole) can affect you. You can use weapons designed for a creature one size larger without penalty. However, your space and reach remain those of a creature of your actual size. The benefits of this ancestry trait stack with the effects of powers, abilities, and spells that change your size category. (3)
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with longswords, rapiers, and short swords, and you treat all firearms as martial weapons. (2)
Total: 11 RP (Advanced)
Alternate Traits
Arcane Officer You gain Arcane Strike as a bonus feat, even if you do not meet the prerequisites—although in such a case, the feat only functions with weapons that you have proficiency with through the weapon familiarity species trait. This trait replaces headfirst charge.
Axe Master You are proficient with the battleaxe, greataxe, and handaxe, and you treat the axe musket, musket, and tomahawk as martial weapons. This trait replaces weapon familiarity.
Bite Instead of careful weapon training, you prefer a more primal method of attack. You can make a bite attack; this is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 damage. This trait replaces weapon familiarity.
Hold Breath You can hold your breath for a number of rounds equal to four times your Constitution score before risking drowning or suffocating. This trait replaces low-light vision.
Stability You gain a +4 species bonus to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground. This trait replaces military training.
Swim You are more comfortable in the water than on land. You have a swim speed of 30 feet and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. This trait replaces headfirst charge.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1/4 to Strength checks to break items while raging and +1/4 to your CMB when attempting sunder maneuvers while raging.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Brawler Add +1/4 to your effective brawler level to determine your unarmed strike damage.
Cavalier Add +1/2 round to the duration of your tactician ability.
Fighter Choose the bull rush or overrun combat maneuver. Add +1/3 to your CMB when attempting this maneuver (maximum bonus of +4).
Gunslinger Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made with firearms (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Magus Add a +1/2 bonus on concentration checks made to cast magus spells defensively.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush and +1/2 to the number of stunning attacks you can attempt per day.
Paladin Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using smite evil (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Psychic Warrior Add +1 to your power points per day.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: battleaxe, greataxe, handaxe, tomahawk, longsword, rapier, short sword, or any type of firearm. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Diplomacy checks to gather information and a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks to demoralize enemies.
Soldier Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt.
Swashbuckler Increase the total number of points in your panache pool by +1/4.
Warpriest Add +1/3 to the number of times per day you can use blessings, but these additional uses must be of blessings that affect weapons or armor.
